plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In the wild, poinsettia grows as a tall shrub or small tree. It is crowned with flame-red bracts that look like petals and surround tiny yellow flower clusters. The bracts glow against dark green leaves in the cool, dry season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter, with peak color in December
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; also grown in gardens and homes worldwide
plants.funFact: The showy red 'petals' are modified leaves called bracts. The true flowers are the small yellow buds at the center. In Mexico, the plant is known as Flor de Nochebuena, or Christmas Eve flower.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Round clusters of trumpet-shaped, sky-blue flowers rise on tall, slender stems above fountains of strappy green leaves. At midsummer they sway over garden borders and along coastal hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, December to February, with a peak around December and January
plants.location: Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, where it is native; widely planted in Southern Hemisphere gardens
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'. Despite the common name, it is not a true lily. It belongs to the amaryllis family.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens silky, blush-pink to white blooms with golden stamens when most of the garden has gone quiet. Its petals scatter like confetti beneath the shrub in cool weather.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, usually October or November through December or January
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, used in cooking and cosmetics in East Asia.
